## PromptLatencyCollector
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
class PromptLatencyCollector(session: AgentSession)
```

`tau_agent_core.latency.PromptLatencyCollector`

Times ``prompt()`` calls on one session and partitions the results.

Usage — the prompt boundary is explicit because it is not recoverable from the
event stream (a ``followUp`` re-entry produces a second full loop bracket inside
the same ``prompt()``, so "one bracket per prompt" is false)::

    collector = PromptLatencyCollector(session)
    with collector.prompt():
        await session.prompt("...")
    ...
    artifact = collector.to_latency_json()

The collector subscribes for its lifetime; call :meth:`close` (or use it as a
context manager) to unsubscribe.

**Constructor parameters**

- `session: AgentSession` — *(no description)*

### prompt

```python
prompt() -> Iterator[None]
```

`tau_agent_core.latency.PromptLatencyCollector.prompt`

Bracket one ``prompt()`` call. Records a sample even if it raises.

A prompt that raised still consumed time and may still have carried a
compaction (``_maybe_auto_compact`` emits its ``agent_end`` from a
``finally`` and then propagates), so dropping the sample would delete
exactly the observations the exclusion exists to catch.

### samples

`tau_agent_core.latency.PromptLatencyCollector.samples: list[PromptLatencySample]`

Every sample, in order. The raw output §9 rule 2 says to look at first.

### to_latency_json

```python
to_latency_json() -> dict[str, Any]
```

`tau_agent_core.latency.PromptLatencyCollector.to_latency_json`

The ``latency.json`` fragment for §5.2's headline number.

Two named populations and no union. There is deliberately no ``"all"`` key
and no method that computes one: a pooled assembled-turn-latency figure over
compacting and non-compacting prompts is the §9 rule 1 failure this module
exists to make unavailable.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — the bracket marker did not hold on this stream. The partition would then be computed from a marker known to be wrong, which is worse than having no artifact.

## PromptLatencySample
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
class PromptLatencySample(index: int, started_ms: int, ended_ms: int, total_ms: int, bare_bracket_ms: int, bare_brackets: int, compactions_committed: int, event_types: tuple[str, ...])
```

`tau_agent_core.latency.PromptLatencySample`

One ``prompt()`` call, timed and classified.

Durations come from ``AgentEvent.timestamp`` (milliseconds, stamped by the
emitting site) rather than from a clock read in this module, so the sample is
measured on the same time base as every other agent-tier stage §9 asks for.

## build_run_manifest
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
build_run_manifest(*, harness: str = HARNESS, compaction_policy: CompactionPolicy, extensions: Sequence[Any] | None = None, **extra: Any) -> dict[str, Any]
```

`tau_agent_core.run_manifest.build_run_manifest`

Build the manifest fragment this harness is responsible for.

``compaction_policy`` is keyword-only and has no default, so a manifest cannot
be built without making the §16.8 decision. That is the whole mechanism: the
option "leave the default" is removed by there not being one.

**Parameters**

- `harness: str = HARNESS` — the harness identity §5.2 partitions latency by. Defaults to :data:`HARNESS`; a pi-era run records ``"pi"`` and the two are different populations that must never be pooled.
- `compaction_policy: CompactionPolicy` — the run's declared policy.
- `extensions: Sequence[Any] | None = None` — the run's loaded extensions, as returned by ``sdk.summarize_extensions()`` (H7, §16.6). ``None`` omits the ``extensions`` key entirely rather than writing an empty list, so a manifest built by a caller that hasn't threaded this through yet is visibly missing the key rather than silently claiming zero extensions loaded.
- `**extra: Any` — *(no description)*

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — ``extra`` contains ``compaction`` or ``extensions``.

## extension_manifest_entries
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
extension_manifest_entries(infos: Sequence[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
```

`tau_agent_core.run_manifest.extension_manifest_entries`

The ``extensions`` manifest fragment (H7, SIM_SPEC_v2 §16.6).

``infos`` is whatever :func:`~tau_agent_core.sdk.summarize_extensions`
returned — accepted structurally (``name``/``path``/``content_hash``/
``subjects``/``tools``/``commands``/``shortcuts``/``hooks`` attributes)
rather than by importing :class:`~tau_agent_core.sdk.ExtensionInfo`, so this
module does not have to import ``sdk`` (which imports ``agent_session``,
which this package's ``__init__`` already loads before ``run_manifest``).

Two runs against the same extension path at different file contents
produce different ``content_hash`` entries here — that is the entire point
(§16.6: "two runs ... at different contents are two experimental
conditions carrying one label").

Provisional shape: §16.6 asks this be built to the same diff format as
tectum's ``T4`` (``tectum-005``), which had not landed as of this writing.
Coordinated through the format when it exists, not guessed at here.

**Parameters**

- `infos: Sequence[Any]` — *(no description)*

## require_compaction_policy
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
require_compaction_policy(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]
```

`tau_agent_core.run_manifest.require_compaction_policy`

Return the manifest's compaction block, or raise.

The read side of the mandatory-partition-key rule. A consumer that reaches for
the policy and finds nothing must stop, not assume: a run whose policy was not
recorded cannot be compared to any other run, and "probably the default" is the
guess §16.8 exists to prevent.

**Parameters**

- `manifest: dict[str, Any]` — *(no description)*

**Raises**

- `KeyError` — ``compaction`` is absent, or ``harness`` is absent — the two are reported together because a compaction policy without a harness identity is only half a partition key.
- `ValueError` — the block is present but not a mode-bearing mapping.

## summarize
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
summarize(values: list[int]) -> dict[str, Any]
```

`tau_agent_core.latency.summarize`

§9's shape: ``median/p90/p99/max, never a single number``.

An empty population reports ``{"n": 0}`` and nothing else. A fabricated zero
median for a population with no members is a value that reads as a measurement.

**Parameters**

- `values: list[int]` — *(no description)*

The check runs on the way out rather than being left to the reader, so an
unlabelled manifest never reaches disk to be trusted later.
